parts.text:
Let me evaluate each option.

W1: In-silico enumeration of capsid–receptor complexes with AlphaFold. Subject: capsid-receptor binding signatures — core of root question. Root asks whether molecular mapping of capsid-receptor interactions can determine transcytosis. W1 asks whether a compact transferable binding-signature class exists — that's basically a sub-question. I'd say SAME.

Stakes: If answered whether a compact transferable binding-signature class exists — that determines whether the whole approach of mapping signatures is viable; choices about which variants to build/collect turn on it. 5? Or 4. The framer mentions it bears on measurability. I'd give 5 — it decides whether to pursue mapping. Reason ≤20 words.

Open: names quantity (model runs/seeds per pair), where published work stops (480 predictions per target), unmeasured range starts within $1000 of GPU reach (seeds beyond 480 are cheap). 5.

Reshape: says sequential "none" — each pair and seed is independent. But the criterion: 5 requires naming a chain that waits step after step plus parallel restructure. Here it says there is no sequential chain — the only parallelism is independent pieces → score 1. Yes, 1.

W2: MD of capsid-glycan-receptor binding and pH dissociation — subject capsid-receptor binding, asks about causal sufficiency of binding energetics for transcytosis. Root asks which variants transcytose vs remain intracellular and for which binding signatures. W2's question is a sub-question-ish (whether binding map is sufficient). Hmm, root question: can molecular mapping determine which variants transcytose and for which signatures. W2 asks whether binding energetics + trafficking kinetics determine transcytosis vs retention — that's arguably a sub-question of the root (whether binding signatures suffice). I'd call it SAME. Actually the root question presumes mapping→prediction; W2 tests sufficiency — a sub-question. SAME.

Stakes: whether binding energetics suffice — answer changes whether to invest in binding maps vs trafficking assays; a choice. 5? Or 4 since one answer (sufficiency likely contested). I'd give 4... The criteria: 5 = a choice someone faces turns on the answer and either answer would move it. Deciding whether to build binding maps or trafficking kinetics assays is a build/scale choice. Give 5.

Open: names quantity (aggregate sampling ensemble × trajectory length), largest reported 2 ms aggregate, unknown above whether ranking changes; no capsid-receptor dissociation free energy published; unmeasured range reachable? $1000 = 250 H100-hours. Aggregate MD sampling beyond 2 ms at 350 ns/day on one GPU — 250 H100-hours ≈ 10 GPU-days ≈ 3.5 µs on one GPU-equivalent. So within reach partially. It names where published measurements stop and the unmeasured range starts within reach. 5.

Reshape: names the chain (time-stepped integration, steps in order), length (2.5–5×10^8 steps), says needs tens-hundreds replicas, one run fills GPU, names restructure (many short replicas pooled in MSM) and condition (rare event likelier from independent starts), and cites source that already tried adaptive ensemble MD + MSM (2 ms). Does cited source already compute this chain in parallel for this system? Different system (protein-protein association, not capsid-receptor). A method published for a different system does not lower score. So the chain is named, length, condition checkable, restructure named; but fails on "one run fills one GPU" and "needs many replicas" → score 3.

W3: Cryo-EM footprints. Subject: capsid-receptor structures; asks whether footprint/resolution resolvable — sub-question of root (measurability of binding signature). SAME.

Stakes: whether cryo-EM can resolve footprints — determines whether to invest in cryo-EM vs other mapping. 4? A choice (which structural method to scale) turns on it. But is it already much more likely one way? Hmm. Give 4.

Open: names quantity (processed particles/classification jobs → resolution), largest30,515 particles 1.86 Å capsid map, unknown whether more particles resolve flexible AAVR PKD densities at 20 Å; reachable with $1000? Processing more particles — more particles require more data collection (not GPU-bound necessarily), but classification compute within reach. I'd say 5? The bottleneck for flexible densities is flexibility not particle count, but scoring based on text: it names quantity, published stop, unmeasured range. Give 5? Or 4 because particle acquisition isn't compute-bought. The criterion is about compute-bought quantity: processed particles/classification jobs buy resolution. Within $1000 reach you could process more particles. I'll give 5.

Hmm, but maybe4 since the unmeasured range (resolving flexible domains) may require far more particles than reachable. Text says unknown whether more particles would resolve. I'll give 4 with reason: flexible-density limit may stem from flexibility, not compute-reachable particle counts. Actually let me be careful — the score asks:5 = names the quantity and where published measurements stop and the unmeasured range starts within that reach. It names quantity and stop (30,515 particles/1.86 Å for capsid; 20 Å tomography). Does unmeasured range start within reach? Processing more particles than 30k — that's easily within 250 H100-hours. So 5.

Reshape: names chain and stages (~a dozen ordered stages), says stages must run in order because each needs previous output; no restructure named, no checkable condition. Score 1? Criterion: 5 requires chain + parallel restructure + checkable condition + no source computing in parallel. 3 = names chain and a way to restructure but one fails. Here no restructure is named at all → 1? The 1 level: "sequential says none, or the only parallelism is independent pieces (copies, a sweep, one job per GPU), or a cited source already computes this chain in parallel." W3 doesn't say none; it names a chain but offers no restructure. Hmm, 1 covers "sequential says none" — not this. It's between 1 and 3. Since no way to restructure is named, it fails the "names the chain and a way to restructure" requirement for 3. I'd give 2? Schema allows 1-5; I'll give 1 with reason: names ordered chain but offers no restructure or checkable condition for parallelism. Hmm, maybe 2. I'll go with 2 (chain named but no restructure). Actually the rubric's 3 requires "names the chain and a way to restructure, but one of these fails..." — no restructure named means below 3. 1's clauses don't fit exactly, but closest is that the only parallelism is independent pieces (half-maps, classification runs) — W3 mentions "several half-map/classification runs per answer" which are independent. So 1.

W4: ML-guided search over capsid sequence space to build the panel. Subject: capsid design/library — different subject from root's mapping of interactions on endothelial cells? Root subject: molecular mapping of capsid-receptor interactions determining transcytosis. W4's subject: sequence-space search and library design — it bears on building the panel for the decisive answer. ADJACENT: same subject (AAV capsids/receptors) but different question (how to design libraries). I'd say ADJACENT.

Stakes: building the panel — a build/collect choice turns on it. But the summary says it's "a known lever" — settled, meaning either answer... Actually stakes: if answered whether ML-guided search yields matched-affinity panels — choice to build panel this way. 4? The compute_open says "settled" meaning known lever, so the answer is already much more likely one way → 3. I'd give 3: answer refines but a known lever already demonstrated.

Open: "settled: wider machine-guided search is a known lever" — names quantity (variant count, yield) but published work covers everything within reach? It says settled → 1? The criterion: 1 = names no compute-bought quantity, or published work already covers everything within that reach. It names quantity (search width / variants) and says known lever with published yield; so published work covers the reachable range → 1.

Reshape: "none: independent per-sequence evaluation" → 1.

W5: Whole-virion atomistic MD. Subject: capsid stability/dynamics — different question: whether binding-altering mutations destabilize capsid. ADJACENT (same subject AAV capsid but different question: fitness/assembly confound). Root subject is capsid-receptor interactions on endothelial cells; W5 is capsid stability. Still AAV capsid variants → ADJACENT.

Stakes: whether a binding signature is physically realisable — refines belief; choices about which mutations to test? Somewhat. But the answer is heavily constrained by physics; likely already expected that big destabilizing mutations fail. 3? I'd give 3.

Open: "settled: whole-virion all-atom MD is already known to be compute-bound" — names quantity (aggregate ns) and where it stops (10 ns), unmeasured range is microseconds on petascale — beyond $1000 reach. So 1: published work covers reachable part; unmeasured range lies beyond reach. Yes, 1.

Reshape: names chain, one run fills GPU, needs handful of runs, only independent replicas parallelize → 3? The 3 level: "names the chain and a way to restructure, but one of these fails: the answer needs many independent runs, so copies side by side already fill the hardware; one run already fills a GPU; or no checkable condition is named." W5 names chain, restructure (replicas on separate nodes), condition (each condition equilibrates independently) — but one run fills a GPU and only a handful of runs. So 3.

W1 reshape: sequential says none — independent predictions → 1.

Distances:
W1: SAME — asks whether a compact transferable binding-signature class exists, a sub-question of root.
W2: SAME — asks whether binding energetics suffice to determine transcytosis vs retention, sub-question.
W3: SAME — asks whether footprints resolvable, sub-question of measurability.
W4: ADJACENT — same subject (AAV capsid variants) but asks library design, not mapping→transcytosis.
W5: ADJACENT — capsid stability confound, different question though same capsid subject.

W1 summary describes root's object of study — root_link counts. All root_links describe the root question's object. Fine.

Now reasons ≤20 words.

W1 stakes (5): "Whether a transferable binding-signature class exists decides whether signature mapping can guide variant choice at all." ~17 words. Good.

W2 stakes (5): "Answer decides whether to scale binding-affinity mapping or invest in trafficking-kinetics assays; both answers move that choice." ~18.

W3 stakes (4): "Decides whether to scale cryo-EM footprint work or switch to alternative mapping; but one route already partly proven." ~19. Hmm. Let me write: "Decides whether to scale cryo-EM for footprints or use other mapping; either answer moves a real build choice." 19 words. Good, value 4.

W4 stakes (3): "Yields shown published; answer refines design-strategy belief but ML-guided diversification is already established as a lever." ~16.

W5 stakes (3): "Answer refines whether binding mutations are physically viable, but destabilising mutations are already expected to be filtered out." ~18.

Open reasons:
W1 (5): "Names runs/seeds per pair; stops at 480 predictions/target; more seeds within $1,000 reach, convergence unknown." 16.
W2 (5): "Names aggregate sampling; stops at 2 ms on another system; capsid-pH dissociation unpublished, sampling within reach." 16.
W3 (5): "Names particles/classification jobs; stops at 30,515 particles for capsid maps; denser classification is within $1,000 reach." 17.
W4 (1): "Says settled — published 201k-variant search already demonstrates the lever, covering the compute-reachable search-width range." 16.
W5 (1): "Settled and compute-bound: only 10 ns reached; microsecond goal needs petascale, far beyond $1,000 reach." 16.

Reshape reasons:
W1 (1): "States no sequential chain: every pair and seed is an independent job; parallelism is only independent copies." 17.
W2 (3): "Names ordered integration and replica-pooled restructure with checkable condition, but one run saturates a GPU and many replicas needed." 20? Count: Names(1) the(2) ordered(3) integration(4) and(5) replica-pooled(6) restructure(7) with(8) checkable(9) condition(10), but(11) one(12) run(13) saturates(14) a(15) GPU(16) and(17) many(18) replicas(19) needed(20). OK 20.
W3 (1): "Names ordered chain but no restructure or checkable condition; only half-map and classification runs run independently." 17.
W4 (1): "Explicitly none — per-sequence scoring is independent, parallelism is only copies across GPUs." 13.
W5 (3): "Names chain and replica restructure, but one run fills a GPU and only a handful of runs needed." 18.

Distance reasons:
W1: "Asks whether a compact transferable capsid–receptor binding-signature class exists — the root's central measurability sub-question." 16.
W2: "Asks whether binding energetics determine transcytosis vs retention — a sufficiency sub-question of the root." 15.
W3: "Asks whether receptor footprints can be resolved molecularly — the root's measurability sub-question about binding signatures." 17.
W4: "Same subject (AAV capsid variants) but asks how to design variant libraries, not whether mapping predicts transcytosis." 18.
W5: "Same capsid subject but asks about capsid stability/assembly confound, a different question from mapping→transcytosis." 16.

Note: "count root_link only if the summary itself describes the root question's object of study" — all summaries describe capsid-receptor interactions, fine.
